findings.location: docs/feature/iis-setup-links/acceptance.md ### S2, the P6 NotTested row ('Both documents already read this way'), against RELEASING.md R-1/R-2 and deploy/k8s/README.md '## Integrations'
findings.obligation: P6: RELEASING.md R-1 and R-2 and deploy/k8s/README.md describe setting up Slack AND Matrix from Instance admin > Integrations in the browser, with the environment settings as the optional operator alternative; expectation E13 adds that an operator 'can finish both integrations by following only those browser instructions'.
findings.observation: Non-blocking for craft; unresolved for completion. I read both documents at ab6fe1b. The Slack half of P6 is already discharged (RELEASING.md:419 R-2 names /admin/instance/integrations, the pasted manifest, the three credentials entered on that page and 'every replica picks it up without a restart'; RELEASING.md:379 marks the SLACK_* trio optional; deploy/k8s/README.md:108 says an instance admin opens /admin/instance/integrations, generates the secrets key and enters the Slack app). The Matrix half is not: grep for Matrix returns exactly one line in each document (RELEASING.md:363 and deploy/k8s/README.md:97), both the same 'Slack and Matrix credentials are sealed under a secrets key' sentence. Neither document tells an operator anywhere that Matrix is connected in the browser, nor where, so an operator who follows only R-1, R-2 and the Kubernetes Integrations section cannot finish Matrix. The S2 acceptance row's claim that 'Both documents already read this way' is therefore true of Slack and the secrets key and false of Matrix, and because the row is NotTested with an examiner owner, no check of this delivery would catch it.
findings.remediation: Choose one and record it before EXAMINE: either add the missing sentence to RELEASING.md R-2 (and the deploy/k8s/README.md Integrations step 4) saying that, once the secrets key exists under Instance admin > Integrations, a workspace admin connects that workspace's own Matrix bot on the workspace integrations page, which is what the shipped instance page already tells its reader; or restate P6 and its S2 row to promise only what the documents do carry for Matrix, namely the secrets key generated in the browser, and leave the workspace-level Matrix connection out of the operator documents. Do not pin either document's prose in a test; the examiner disposition stays correct either way.

Semantic RED observed, not infrastructure. In /Users/jeffbailey/.cache/nwdes/iis-setup-links/s2-red.txt the failing step is inside 'Scenario: The Slack setup guide names the browser form and asks for no restart': the page answered 200 OK with text/html at /workspace/integrations/slack/setup and its whole rendered text is printed, and the panic is that locked sentence 1 'An instance admin enters the app's Client ID, Client Secret and Signing Secret under Instance admin > Integrations.' is nowhere on it. 16 scenarios (15 passed, 1 failed), 163 steps (162 passed, 1 failed), 0 parsing errors, 0 hook errors. The printed body is the shipped crates/foundry-app/templates/integrations/slack_setup.html, whose step 3 still says 'set SLACK_CLIENT_ID, SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET and SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET on this Foundry' and step 4 still says 'Restart Foundry.'. So the RED is the missing production behaviour P4 promises, reached through a served page, and not an import error, a missing fixture, a cross-root path mismatch or a provider mismatch.

Locked copy fidelity is byte-exact. The three rows of the scenario's sentence table were compared character by character against the I-20 row of docs/feature/instance-integration-setup/discuss/user-stories.md line 167: each table row equals the locked sentence exactly, the only difference being the locked row's list numbering prefixes '3. ' and '4. ', which the acceptance row explicitly declares not to be the observation ('not which list item or markup carries each one'). The U+203A guillemet in 'Instance admin > Integrations', the ASCII apostrophes and the semicolon in the footnote all match. Expectations E9 and E10 are therefore observable word for word by the recorded oracle, and the footnote's lowercase 'and restart' does not collide with the absent-phrase check for 'Restart Foundry'.

Public driving port, constructible, independent, complete for P4's prose clause. The stimulus is a real GET of /workspace/integrations/slack/setup through the production router in process with real Postgres, as the reader the S1 offer actually sends there (Tomas Rivera, a workspace admin who is not this Foundry's instance admin); no private module, no handler call and no test-fabricated string is asserted. All scaffolding the oracle needs already exists at this commit: the step helper sentences() reads the one-column table, eip::WorkspaceDoor::parse('the Slack setup page') is a shipped arm (crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/external_integration_plugins.rs:462 and :3819) and the page text comes from tm::page_text via eip::text, so the oracle is constructible before craft. Chain per obligation: stimulus (that GET) -> expected observation (the three locked sentences in reading order, read with a cursor that only advances, plus the two absent phrases) -> falsifier (any sentence missing or out of order, or either phrase present), which is exactly the falsifier the slice declares.

Both absence assertions are non-vacuous and carry a discriminator. then_reads_nothing_saying first asserts the page answered and reads the same rendered text that the ordering assertion positively searched, so a page nobody read, an error answer or an empty body cannot satisfy it: looked-and-absent is told apart from never-looked. Neither phrase is vacuously absent today: the shipped template contains 'Restart Foundry.' in step 4 and 'SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET on this Foundry' in step 3, which the printed RED body confirms, so each check can fail on the current page and each would fail on a page that gained the new sentences while keeping the old instruction. Scope note retained, not a defect: the check is a case-sensitive literal over the whole rendered page rather than over the steps alone, which is exactly the falsifier the slice declares ('the phrase Restart Foundry anywhere in the page's steps'); it is stricter than the promise in reach and narrower in spelling, and no compliant I-20 page can be refused by it.

P4's manifest clause is covered by reuse, with its stated limitation retained. The cited scenario 'With a secrets key the page shows what to paste into Slack' (feature line 77) asserts at line 84 'the manifest shown equals the one on the Slack setup page' and separately pins this Foundry's own return and events addresses at line 83. That is precisely the declared falsifier for this slice ('a manifest that differs from the instance integrations page's'), and the slice's declared impact is prose-only in one template with the manifest field and its handler untouched, so no prose-only implementation of S2 can lose the outcome undetected. Expectation E11's own limitation stands unresolved by design and is not an oracle defect: nothing compares the rendered manifest against a previously published copy, because the handoff supplies no such copy; a later change to the shared handler field would move both pages together and stay invisible to an equality observation.

P6's NotTested disposition is the right treatment, and I read both documents. RELEASING.md R-1 (line 404) and R-2 (line 419) already tell an operator that an instance admin opens /admin/instance/integrations, presses Generate for the secrets key, pastes the rendered manifest at api.slack.com and enters Client ID, Client Secret and Signing Secret on that same page, where 'every replica picks it up without a restart'; line 379 documents the SLACK_* trio as 'Optional: the Slack app entered in the UI is used otherwise'. deploy/k8s/README.md step 4 (line 108) says an instance admin opens /admin/instance/integrations, generates the secrets key and enters the Slack app. So the Slack half and the optional-alternative half of P6 already read as promised. Treating these as NotTested with an examiner owner is correct rather than evasive: they are repository documents no public address of this Foundry renders, and pinning their sentences would freeze prose the product never promised word for word. The residual Matrix gap is recorded as a finding.

diagnostic: Accepted: the S2 public oracle is adequate, constructible and independent, and its RED is semantic. P4's prose clause has one falsifiable chain through the real public port (GET /workspace/integrations/slack/setup in production composition, read by the workspace admin the S1 offer actually sends there): the three locked I-20 sentences are asserted byte-exact against docs/feature/instance-integration-setup/discuss/user-stories.md:167 and in reading order by a cursor that only advances, and the two absent-phrase checks are non-vacuous today and carry their discriminator, because the same answered page is positively read for the sentences it must contain. P4's manifest clause is covered by reuse of the shipped manifest-equality scenario (feature:84), which is exactly the declared falsifier for a prose-only slice; E11's own limitation that no previously published manifest exists to compare against is design's stated limit, not an oracle defect. P6 is NotTested with an examiner owner, which is the right treatment for two repository documents the product never renders, and its Slack and optional-alternative halves already read as promised; one non-blocking design finding records that neither document carries any Matrix browser instruction, so P6's Matrix clause and E13 stay unresolved completion obligations. No new execution: HEAD is ab6fe1b with a clean tree and the selected oracle and support bytes are byte-identical to those committed there, so the acceptance designer's recorded lane run at that same revision is the current evidence (us-iis-04: 16 scenarios, 15 passed, 1 failed at the I-20 sentence; instance-integration-setup: 75, 74 passed, 1 failed; check-arch passed). typesafe: unavailable, so all judgements here are my own local reasoning; no timing claim is made and none is owed.
